To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the organizational model is a useful tool to support information security specification.
the use of a well-defined organizational model of information security can significantly improve the specification of functional security requirements.

the organizational model of security requirements can be used to: (1) group security requirements into different levels and layers, (2) express the dependencies between requirements, (3) express the dependencies and relationships among security requirements, security controls, and security services, (4) express the dependencies of security requirements to other functional requirements, (5) express the relationships among different types of security requirements and security requirements, and (6) provide an efficient and effective way to specify security requirements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the specification of information security requirements, and the use of organizational models to support such specifications.
the specification of information security requirements of information and communication systems.
how the information security requirements for an organization can be modeled in order to provide an efficient and effective specification of the requirements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a proper organization of information security requirements can be established by the following: 1) identifying the information security goals of the organization; 2) identifying the security requirements for each information asset in the organization; and 3) identifying the relationships between information assets.
the model proposed in this paper is capable of supporting a wide range of security requirements in a flexible way.
the model is a powerful and flexible framework that can be used for specifying information security requirements in many different types of information systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed framework is a model for expressing information security requirements that are organized into layers of abstraction.

the proposed framework can be used as a tool for specifying security requirements in a structured manner, and the resulting specifications would be more comprehensible and more amenable to verification.
organizational models can be used as the foundation for developing information security requirements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizational modeling of security is a powerful approach for dealing with information systems security requirements.
the use of organizational modeling in security requirements engineering can be used to address the challenges of expressing information security requirements.
organizational modeling can be a powerful tool in the specification of information security.
